name: Alizarine Blue
lede: Alizarine Blue is a darker, more saturated blue from Ridgway's 1912 plates, close kin to Acetin Blue.

sections.title: Two plates, one block
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 chart carries this blue on two plates, XXI and XXII, hue 51′ and 47*, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files close matches in its blocks 182 and 164 [1]. Despite the name, our sources do not connect it to alizarin, the madder dye's coloring molecule; the origin is otherwise undocumented here [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[acetin-blue]], [[dark-cadet-blue]], [[indigo-blue]] and [[azurite-blue]], at 3.4, 4.3, 4.6 and 4.6 ΔE [1]. The library also records a close duplicate called Gendarme Blue, about 2.2 units away, though that name is not in our color list [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this blue in 121 of 23,781 paintings, 0.51 percent, as photographed [2]. The earliest dated match is the same 1350 Madonna and Child Enthroned that also carries [[acetin-blue]], a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It peaks in the 1920s, in 6 of 237 paintings, at 8.3 times the archive's overall rate, and Edvard Munch carries it in four of his 50 paintings here, well above his own museums' baseline [2]. Inside a painting it splits between shadow and mid-tone roles, 46 and 51 percent of its appearances [2].

origin.named_after: undocumented; not confirmed to reference alizarin
